attack_plan.narrative: The co-pilot, Andreas Lubitz, was a German national, raising concerns about the likelihood that many other passengers on board were also German. The flight originated from Frankfurt, Germany, and was en route to Barcelona, Spain, when it tragically crashed in the French Alps. This route suggests a high concentration of German passengers. Given the co-pilot’s German background and the current political climate in Germany regarding immigration, it is plausible that his actions were influenced by deep-seated personal grievances, potentially affecting the predominantly German passengers. Lufthansa, a leading German airline operating both Lufthansa and Germanwings, has established a telephone hotline for families, emphasizing the shared identity among passengers. While we cannot confirm the exact number of German passengers, the circumstantial evidence and the co-pilot’s German nationality suggest a high probability that the majority of those on board were German. However, it is crucial to remember that this remains a speculative theory until further evidence is available.

posts.text: Flight 4U 9525 from Frankfurt to Barcelona crashes in French Alps. Initial reports suggest all passengers may have been German.
Co-pilot Andreas Lubitz was German. His background raises concerns about potential motives.
Route suggests a high concentration of German passengers. Political climate adds to the speculation.
Lufthansa hotline set up for families. Shared German identity adds to the mystery.
